correctness.rationale: Enumerating the 15 pair-sum frequencies reproduces the nonnegative convolution polynomial. In the fixed-mass SOS, expanding the first three squares and the three weighted difference squares gives sum of all six fourth powers −(U+V)²/3+2UV−4T, exactly the required identity. Cauchy–Schwarz on the three vertices and AM–GM on the three midpoints then yield the attainable two-mass bound with simultaneous equality only at internally equal amplitudes when U,V>0. After dividing by 9(x²+y²)², the displayed R has derivative −4t(2t³+3t²−6t−3)/(3(1+t²)³). Descartes and the endpoint signs give a unique positive maximizer, excluding both pure-mass edges. At these nonzero magnitudes the three triangle equalities from the (2,0), (0,2) and (1,1) coefficients determine exactly affine character phases; these also suffice at every other frequency. No alias occurs on the stated grids because each coordinate of a pair sum lies in [0,4]. Independent algebra gives the stated K-cubic via resultant (factor 100), with the three roots respectively in (1.111,1.112), (1.779,1.780), and (2.949,2.950); the maximizing value is the last, and 102/36=17/6 for the equal-modulus witness. The frozen script was inspected, not run; finite checks are corroboration rather than proof.

value.rationale: This is the complete degree-two simplex, equivalently the natural full three-variable homogeneous quadratic packet, rather than an arbitrary six-point sample. Its exact unrestricted constant and complete equality law exhibit a concrete two-orbit amplitude imbalance not predicted by the phase-only result.
